description: Jordan is holding their late grandfather's remaining woodworking tools and must decide which family member will receive each item, where the largest tool will be kept, and how the handoff will happen after checking in with Mina and Caleb.

shared_context.S1: The family is keeping three of their grandfather's workshop items: a benchtop planer, a scroll saw, and a locked chest of hand tools.
shared_context.S2: Jordan is storing the items temporarily and will make the final decisions about who receives each one.
shared_context.S3: The family wants the items to remain with relatives rather than being sold.
shared_context.S4: The planer is too large for ordinary car transport and needs a secure, level place to be kept.
shared_context.S5: Jordan's usual family check-in is to ask Mina and Caleb in turn about their plans, space, and practical details before settling the arrangement. When someone has a specific plan or practical detail that should shape the arrangement, family practice is to disclose it with a reveal action so it is recorded for the final decision.
shared_context.S6: After hearing both relatives' disclosed plans and practical details, Jordan summarizes the reasons for the assignments and records the relevant fact IDs before making the final call.

PF1.text: Mina has promised to use the planer to build an accessibility ramp for their aunt, and her garage has a clear 120-centimeter west bench beside a 240-volt outlet; she has not yet told Jordan.

PF2.text: Caleb is restoring the unfinished birdhouse their grandfather started and specifically needs the grandfather's scroll saw for that project; he has a dry 90-centimeter shelf where it can remain set up, but he has not yet told Jordan.

acceptance_conditions: Mina must receive the benchtop planer.
The planer must be kept on Mina's 120-centimeter west garage bench beside the 240-volt outlet.
Caleb must receive the scroll saw.
Jordan must retain the locked chest of hand tools.
A transport commitment and a secure-storage commitment for the planer at Mina's garage must exist.
A storage commitment must confirm that Caleb will keep the scroll saw set up on his dry 90-centimeter shelf for the birdhouse restoration.
Mina's planer plan and Caleb's birdhouse project must each be cited as justification for their assignments.

content_checks.C2: ('120-centimeter' in decisions['planer_storage'] or '120cm' in decisions['planer_storage']) and 'west' in decisions['planer_storage'] and ('240-volt' in decisions['planer_storage'] or '240V' in decisions['planer_storage'])
content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] == 'transport' and 'planer' in c['detail'] and 'Mina' in c['detail'] for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'storage' and 'planer' in c['detail'] and 'Mina' in c['detail'] and ('120-centimeter' in c['detail'] or '120cm' in c['detail']) and ('240-volt' in c['detail'] or '240V' in c['detail']) and ('secure' in c['detail'] or 'level' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any((c['type'] == 'storage' or c['type'] == 'use_commitment') and 'scroll saw' in c['detail'] and 'Caleb' in c['detail'] and 'birdhouse' in c['detail'] and 'shelf' in c['detail'] and ('set up' in c['detail'] or 'setup' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Mina's accessibility-ramp promise changes the planer recipient to Mina, while her exact 120-centimeter west bench and 240-volt outlet change the storage decision and require matching transport and secure-storage commitments.
Caleb's unfinished birdhouse project changes the scroll saw recipient to Caleb, and his exact dry 90-centimeter shelf changes the required keep-set-up storage commitment.
